note: Starter dataset summarizing published NASA microgravity combustion investigations. Metrics are representative values compiled from public literature and MUST be verified against PSI data files (verified=false). Regenerate/extend with scripts/build_dataset.py.

investigations.name: SoFIE-GEL
investigations.title: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction — Growth and Extinction Limits
keyFindings: Flames spread over PMMA at oxygen concentrations as low as ~15% in quiescent microgravity — below typical Earth extinction limits (~17–18%).
In very low flow, flame spread is limited by radiative heat loss rather than oxygen supply, producing a distinct extinction boundary.
Two extinction regimes exist: oxygen-limit extinction at high flow and blow-off/radiative extinction at low flow.
safetyImplications: Materials qualified as 'low flammability' on Earth can sustain flame spread in spacecraft cabins — qualification limits must be re-derived for microgravity.
Weak forced ventilation may not extinguish a flame; both high-flow and quiescent regimes need fire-response procedures.
objectives: Map the ignition and extinction boundaries of flame spread over flat solid fuels in sustained microgravity.
Test whether materials qualified as low-flammability on Earth remain non-propagating in µg.
investigations.apparatus: CIR flat solid-fuel holder — thin PMMA sheets in an opposed-flow duct

investigations.name: BASS-II
investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids II
keyFindings: Characterized opposed-flow flame spread and extinction over small solid samples across oxygen and flow regimes.
Observed transitions from steady burning to abrupt extinction that are absent in normal gravity.
Elevated oxygen (as in proposed exploration atmospheres) markedly increases burning rate and delays extinction.
safetyImplications: Suppression strategies relying on airflow changes must account for non-monotonic extinction behavior.
Elevated-O2 exploration atmospheres widen the flammable envelope for common spacecraft solids.
objectives: Measure opposed-flow flame spread and extinction over small solid samples across O2 and ventilation regimes.
Characterize µg-unique transitions: steady burn → abrupt extinction → smolder.
investigations.apparatus: MSG modular flow duct with fan — spheres, slabs and sheets on a sample holder

varied: sample form/size (1–2 cm spheres, slabs, sheets)

investigations.name: FLEX / FLEX-2
investigations.title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
keyFindings: Discovered sustained 'cool flame' chemistry: droplets kept burning invisibly at ~600 K long after the visible hot flame extinguished.
Cool flames can consume a large fraction of remaining fuel and persist for tens of seconds undetected.
Two-stage extinction means visible flameout is not a reliable indicator that combustion has stopped.
safetyImplications: Post-extinction monitoring is essential: fuel vapor can keep reacting and re-ignite or generate CO after 'extinguishment'.
Fire detection must not rely on visible/UV flame signatures alone; gas-phase and thermal sensors are needed.
objectives: Map flammability limits of isolated fuel droplets and quantify gaseous suppressant effectiveness — CO2, He and N2 dilution.
Measure droplet burning rates, extinction diameters and post-flameout cool-flame chemistry in quiescent µg.
investigations.apparatus: CIR Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) — free-floating ~1–4 mm droplets

investigations.name: ACME
investigations.title: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments
keyFindings: Mapped soot inception and growth in laminar coflow diffusion flames without buoyancy-driven distortion.
Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) showed gas burners can mimic solid-fuel burning rates for material testing.
Electric fields and flame design parameters demonstrably alter flame shape, soot, and extinction.
safetyImplications: Soot production physics in microgravity informs smoke detector placement and post-fire contamination cleanup.
BRE enables ground testing of spacecraft material flammability without drop towers.
objectives: Measure structure, soot inception and extinction of laminar coflow diffusion flames without buoyant distortion.
Emulate solid-fuel burning rates with a gas burner (BRE) to enable ground-based flammability testing.
investigations.apparatus: CIR coflow burner — gaseous fuel jet in coflowing oxidizer (E-FIELD adds high-voltage mesh electrodes)

investigations.name: Saffire I–VI
investigations.title: Spacecraft Fire Experiment
keyFindings: Largest deliberate fires ever set in an uncrewed spacecraft — flame behavior at ~meter scale differs from small CIR samples.
Concurrent (downstream) flame spread is dramatically faster than opposed (upstream) spread and is the dominant hazard mode.
Provided remote measurements of flame spread, material flammability, O2 consumption and CO/CO2 production in a real vehicle.
safetyImplications: Small-scale flammability tests underpredict large-scale fire growth — vehicle-level factors (flow, fuel area) matter.
Post-fire atmosphere data calibrates how long a crewed vehicle remains uninhabitable after a large fire.
objectives: Observe a realistic large-scale fire inside an uncrewed cargo vehicle after departure from the ISS.
Measure flame spread, material flammability, O2 draw-down and CO/CO2 production at vehicle scale.
investigations.apparatus: Cygnus pressurized volume — instrumented flow duct and large material panels

investigations.name: SAME
investigations.title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment
keyFindings: Measured particle size distribution of smoke from overheated and ignited spacecraft materials.
Microgravity smoke particles are significantly larger and more agglomerated than Earth smoke — no sedimentation to remove them.
Different materials produce distinct aerosol signatures useful for source identification.
safetyImplications: ISS smoke detectors must be calibrated for larger particle sizes — Earth-calibrated detectors can under-detect.
Aerosol signature libraries could enable detector discrimination between nuisance sources and real fires.
objectives: Measure the size distribution and concentration of smoke particles from overheated and ignited spacecraft materials.
Benchmark real smoke-detector response against reference aerosol instruments in µg.
investigations.apparatus: MSG sealed aerosol chamber — heated material samples on a carousel

varied: material (Teflon, Kapton, Pyrell foam, silicone rubber, cellulose)

investigations.name: Confined Combustion
investigations.title: Confined Combustion — Flame Spread in Confined Volumes
keyFindings: Flame spread between close parallel plates (confined geometry, like racks/ducts) is strongly affected by wall heat recirculation.
Exploration-like atmospheres (reduced pressure, elevated O2 mole fraction) change spread rate non-linearly.
Narrow gaps can either accelerate flames via heat feedback or quench them via heat loss — a critical design parameter.
safetyImplications: Equipment racks, cable trays and duct geometries must be assessed for confinement-enhanced fire spread.
Exploration habitat atmospheres cannot be certified with sea-level flammability data.
objectives: Quantify how confinement — parallel plates, rack and duct gaps — changes flame spread versus open µg tests.
Measure spread under exploration-like atmospheres: reduced pressure with elevated O2 fraction.
investigations.apparatus: CIR confined-channel rig — twin parallel plates with adjustable gap

investigations.name: FLARE
investigations.title: Flammability Limit At Reduced-g Experiment
keyFindings: Directly maps material flammability limits at Lunar (0.17 g) and Martian (0.38 g) gravity using an on-orbit centrifuge.
Partial gravity restores some buoyant convection — flammability limits sit between microgravity and Earth values but not on a simple line.
Designed to feed directly into Artemis/Gateway and Mars transit fire-safety requirements.
safetyImplications: Fire safety for Moon/Mars missions cannot be interpolated naively from ISS and Earth data — partial-g limits are needed.
Centrifuge-based partial-g testing is the only way to obtain these limits long-duration.
objectives: Map material flammability limits directly at lunar (0.17 g) and martian (0.38 g) gravity.
Provide the partial-g data anchor that ISS and Earth results cannot interpolate.
investigations.apparatus: Kibo module combustion cell mounted on a centrifuge — selectable g level

investigations.name: BASS
investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids
keyFindings: Showed that sample geometry and form factor — sphere diameter, sheet thickness, candle vs slab — shift extinction boundaries in µg even when the polymer is unchanged.
Observed transitions from flaming to smoldering combustion that have no normal-gravity counterpart.
122 PSI-26 test runs are normalized in this dataset — see the experiment_run records.
safetyImplications: Fire-safety models must carry geometry as a first-class parameter — the same polymer can extinguish or persist depending on form factor.
Smolder transitions mean post-flame monitoring is required even after visible burn-out.
objectives: Quantify burning and extinction behavior of solid fuels in opposed and concurrent forced flow inside the MSG duct.
Isolate the effect of sample geometry and size on µg flammability limits.
investigations.apparatus: MSG modular flow duct with fan — spheres, slabs, sheets and candles on a sample tree

varied: fuel and form factor (1–2 cm spheres, slabs, sheets, candles)

investigations.name: SAME-R
investigations.title: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment — Reflight
keyFindings: Reflew the SAME diagnostic stack on the SAME flight hardware to extend µg smoke-particle statistics and validate the lognormal size-distribution assumption used by the moment method.
Compared ionization and photoelectric detector responses against reference aerosol instruments on the same microgravity smoke.
Public PSI release PSI-101 (2024) packages the reflight dataset.
safetyImplications: Extends the calibration basis for next-generation smoke detectors on Gateway and lunar habitats.
Confirms Earth-calibrated detectors need µg-specific particle-size correction before deployment in exploration cabins.
objectives: Extend SAME smoke-aerosol measurements to additional materials and longer smoke aging.
Validate detector-response models required for next-generation spacecraft smoke detectors.
investigations.apparatus: SAME hardware reflight — sealed aerosol chamber with sample carousel

investigations.name: SPICE
investigations.title: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
keyFindings: Determined laminar smoke points — the largest soot-free flame — for non-buoyant gas-jet flames.
Smoke points proved substantially different in reduced gravity than in normal gravity; increasing coflow velocity or decreasing burner diameter raises the µg smoke point.
Hardware lineage runs SPICE → SLICE → ACME CLD Flame, chaining the coflow dataset.
safetyImplications: Sooting-propensity data feeds fire-spread and contamination models — soot carries most of a fire's radiant heat and drives detector loading.
Gas-jet flame data covers the leak-and-ignite scenario inside ducted hardware.
objectives: Measure smoke-point properties of non-buoyant jet diffusion flames across fuels and nozzle/coflow configurations.
Provide soot-inception data to validate combustion and fire-spread models.
investigations.apparatus: MSG enclosed coflow burner — gas jet inside a coaxial oxidizer stream

investigations.name: SLICE
investigations.title: Structure & Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
keyFindings: Captured a unique coflow-jet dataset spanning weak near-extinction flames to strong heavily-sooting flames.
µg flames destabilize at higher forced airflows — the 0g/1g liftoff-flow difference is comparable to the 1g buoyant velocity.
Lower flame temperatures and dramatically higher soot concentrations than normal-gravity twins on the same hardware.
safetyImplications: Flame attachment/stability physics governs whether a flame stays anchored at a leak point or propagates downstream through ducts.
Soot-rich µg flames sharpen the contamination case for post-fire cleanup requirements.
objectives: Determine laminar diffusion flame structure and liftoff (stabilization) limits as functions of fuel and burner diameter.
Provide a validation dataset for combustion models including radiation, soot and detailed kinetics.
investigations.apparatus: MSG coflow burner (SPICE heritage) — fuel jet in coflowing air

investigations.name: ACME E-FIELD Flames
investigations.title: ACME — Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Flames
keyFindings: Applied electric fields to flame ions — the resulting ion wind mimics buoyant convection, giving a controllable body-force 'gravity knob' between 0g and 1g behavior.
Field polarity and voltage measurably reshape the flame, shift soot production and move extinction boundaries.
21 PSI-22 runs are normalized in this dataset — see the experiment_run records.
safetyImplications: Partial-gravity fire behavior (Moon 0.17 g, Mars 0.38 g) can be bracketed on-orbit without a centrifuge — complements FLARE.
Ion-wind suppression is a candidate clean extinguishment mechanism for habitats.
objectives: Quantify how electric fields modify laminar flame structure, soot and extinction via ion wind.
Use the field as a controllable body-force analog to interpolate flame behavior between 0g and 1g.
investigations.apparatus: CIR coflow burner with high-voltage mesh electrodes around the flame

investigations.name: ACME CFI / CFI-G
investigations.title: ACME — Cool Flames Investigation (with Gases)
keyFindings: Largest single corpus in this dataset — 333 PSI-159 runs mapping the boundary between no-ignition, oxygen-limit extinction and sustained burnout for gaseous alkanes.
Systematically varied fuel species and dilution (100% → 30–50%) to bracket where cool and hot flames survive at elevated O2.
Cool-flame events documented within the run matrix — extending FLEX droplet results to gaseous fuels.
safetyImplications: The no-ignition/extinction/burnout boundary is the operational map for leak scenarios in fuel-handling hardware.
Fuel dilution is as sharp a safety lever as O2 control — relevant to inerting procedures after a leak.
objectives: Map ignition, extinction and cool-flame boundaries of gaseous alkane flames in a spherical burner.
Quantify the effect of fuel dilution on flammability limits at elevated O2.
investigations.apparatus: CIR spherical gaseous burner — ignition at the center of a quiescent chamber
